solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Out cold, come to as arranged

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the three words before it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone knocked out cold is urged to wake up and come round as planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone out cold is unconscious, in a deep coma-like state.

clue.text: State one's business — it's material

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for the US state of California
one is the Roman numeral I
CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to declare their trade, which turns out to be fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a plain cotton cloth, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Can go round ravine taking right working parts

indicators.note: go round says the first piece surrounds the rest

parts.note: can, meaning is allowed to, is may
a chine is a deep narrow ravine, a word found in southern English place names

explanation.surface: A tin rolls around a gorge, taking the right route.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the moving components of an engine or device collectively form its mechanism.

clue.text: Northern god's anterior point

indicators.note: anterior means placed before, so the god's name comes ahead of the other piece

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: The front tip of a Norse deity's weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a prickle on a rose is a sharp spike or point.

clue.text: Dish from southern Britain and two from Rome embracing Asian beast

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for Britain

indicators.note: embracing says the numeral's letters hug the beast between them

parts.note: two in Roman numerals is II
the yak is a Himalayan ox

explanation.surface: A meal from the south of Britain and Italy featuring an Asian animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Japanese hotpot of thinly sliced beef and vegetables is a dish.

clue.text: That which provided speculation?

parts.note: 'that which' can be replaced by 'what', as in 'I saw what you did'
provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'

explanation.surface: A question about what something supplied by way of guesswork.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a hypothetical, so it stands for a piece of speculation; the question mark flags the loose equivalence.

clue.text: Hail even masks start of wild night of pranks

indicators.note: masks says the outer pieces hide another letter within them

parts.note: hallo is a greeting, a hail
e'en is a poetic contraction of evening, written as even here

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Hailstones even hide the beginning of a wild evening of mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' is the archaic noun for evening, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: On 31 October, children play tricks, so it is a night traditionally given to mischief.

clue.text: Having ups and downs in liquidity

definitions.text: Having ups and downs in liquidity

parts.words: Having ups and downs in liquidity
parts.note: liquidity suggests finance, but it means water, which rises and falls with the moon

explanation.surface: A company's cash flow is volatile.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea rises and falls twice daily, so water with such rising and falling is described this way.

clue.text: Pal losing rag initially — his indisposition is extremely unpleasant

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the word for pal

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word rag
indisposition means the word his is out of sorts, its letters disordered

explanation.surface: A friend without a cloth suffers an illness that is very nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops R from FRIEND to give FIEND; 'indisposition' rearranges HIS to ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something devilishly cruel or awful is extremely unpleasant.

clue.text: Speaking part

parts.note: suggests a role with lines in a play, but means the part of the body used for speaking

explanation.surface: An actor's role with lines to deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: The lips and tongue form the organ of speech, the bodily part that speaks.

clue.text: One unwittingly suffers from it

parts.note: unwittingly literally means without wit or knowing, so the thing suffered is not knowing

explanation.surface: Something a person endures without realising it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unwitting is to be unaware, which is exactly having no awareness or information of something.

clue.text: Pot smoker?

parts.note: suggests a cannabis user, but the pot is a ... pot on a roof, through which smoke rises

explanation.surface: Someone who smokes cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like drug slang; here it is the clay pot on top of a flue, and the thing that smokes is the flue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A flue carrying smoke up from a fire ends in a chimney pot, so it is literally what smokes at the pot.

clue.text: Did the rounds — Pa went missing and did some fishing

indicators.note: went missing says the named letters disappear from the longer word

parts.note: a guard who did the rounds patrolled
taken as written, a word for father

explanation.surface: Dad walked his usual route, then disappeared off to go fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a moving boat.

clue.text: Be said to be made to order

parts.note: taken as written
said is the past tense of say, as is spoke

explanation.surface: A garment reportedly made to the customer's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tailoring cut for an individual customer, such as a suit, is custom-made rather than off the peg.

clue.text: Nut disintegrates as I chop it

indicators.note: disintegrates says the following words break apart and are reassembled

explanation.surface: A nut crumbles as the cook chops it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a green kernel from an Asian tree is a nut.

clue.text: Blunder mismatches some skin

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Clumsy errors lead to badly paired skin, as in a botched graft.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the layer of tissue beneath the epidermis is the true skin, so the word stands for skin.

clue.text: Noble cabby

parts.note: a nobleman is a man of high rank, but a taxi driver waits at a taxi rank

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who drives a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an aristocrat, and punningly a fellow who waits at a taxi stand.

clue.text: Beadle is struggling having been let down

indicators.note: struggling suggests the words beadle and is thrashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: A parish officer is in trouble after being disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: A beadle was a minor parish or church official.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: someone lowered down a cliff on a rope has descended that way.

clue.text: Mother is over the line

indicators.note: over, as in turned over, says the letters of mother and is are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mum has gone beyond the limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: on a weather map, a contour joining places of equal temperature is a line.

clue.text: High-spirited lad is hard on pencils

parts.note: a lad is a boy
taken as written
H marks a hard lead on a pencil, as in HB or 2H

explanation.surface: An energetic youngster is rough on his pencils, wearing them down.
explanation.definitionFit: Being high-spirited is youthful exuberance, the lively manner of a young lad.

clue.text: So I might take one over the eight? That would be daft

parts.note: so can mean as, as in 'so far' / 'as far'
one more than eight is nine; the phrase is also British slang for one drink too many

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders whether to have one too many, which would be foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for being slightly drunk; here it is read literally as the number after eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something daft is silly or stupid, like a donkey proverbially is.

clue.text: A bed in France may be gloomy

parts.note: un is French for a
lit is the French word for bed

explanation.surface: A French bed may be dark and dismal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a room with no lamps on is dark and gloomy.

clue.text: Individual enthralled by disc being copied

indicators.note: enthralled by says the first piece is captured inside the disc

parts.note: CD is a compact disc
individual, meaning single, is lone

explanation.surface: A person captivated by a record that is being pirated.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something duplicated as a genetic replica has been copied exactly.

clue.text: Account for former wife getting even

parts.note: a former wife is an ex
even means flat or level, which is plain in the sense of a flat stretch

explanation.surface: Justifying an ex-wife's taking revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to account for something is to give the reasons for it, making it clear.

clue.text: Drop round

definitions.meaning: to fall or set down heavily and suddenly

explanation.surface: An instruction to drop in on a round.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to fall heavily and to be rotund.

clue.text: One French flute played outside in musical

indicators.note: outside says the scrambled letters wrap around the other piece
played suggests the word flute is performed in a different arrangement of its letters

parts.note: un is French for one

explanation.surface: A Frenchman plays the flute out of doors in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'musical' looks like the noun, a stage show; it is the adjective meaning melodious. 'played' scrambles the flute to TEFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something musical is melodious and pleasant to hear.

clue.text: Man going up, lady coming down

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the man's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Aidan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man ascends while a woman descends, like a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming down' is how the answer reads in the grid; the lady's name read upwards is the man's.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a woman's first name, so it stands for a lady.

clue.text: Agile kid ran with haul, about to crack up

indicators.note: about signals the letters of the fodder are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A nimble youngster ran off with the loot, about to have a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the fodder; the British idiom means to laugh loudly and coarsely.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to crack up is to burst into helpless laughter, which the British phrase describes as raucous guffawing.

clue.text: Employment department's plan to find position

parts.note: DE was the abbreviation for the UK Department of Employment
a ploy is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: A government jobs ministry has a scheme to find someone a post.
explanation.walkthrough: The Department of Employment was a British government ministry, abbreviated DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to position troops or resources is to put them into place ready for action.

clue.text: Set sail from bay in eastern sea

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
to bay is to bark, as a hound does

explanation.surface: A ship heads off from a bay on an eastern sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like a coastal inlet but is the dog's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to set sail is to board ship and begin a voyage.
